correctness.rationale: The circulant, up to transpose, is multiplication by a=(1+X)^n−1 in the odd-order quotient Z₂[X]/(X^n−1). One can verify the Smith conclusion without a splitting field. For n=2^r−1 the factors X−1 and H=(X^n−1)/(X−1) are coprime modulo two since H(1)=n is odd, giving an integral 2-adic product. At X=1 the multiplier is odd. On the H factor, 1+X is a unit; repeated squaring modulo four gives (1+X)^(2^r)≡1+X^(2^r)+2X^(2^(r−1)). As X^(2^r)=X there, (1+X)a≡2X^(2^(r−1)) modulo four. Thus multiplication by a on the rank n−1 summand is twice an invertible integral map. At n=1 that summand is absent. For n=2^r+1, a reduces modulo two to 1+X+X^(−1) in the cyclic quotient (using Frobenius and X^n=1). Its only possible common factor with X^n−1 is X²+X+1, occurring exactly when 3 divides n, i.e. r odd. The cyclic polynomial is squarefree modulo two. In that case split off the integral cubic-root factor X²+X+1; on its rank-two summand a=(−X²)^n−1=−2, and a is a unit on the complement. These integral arguments give the exact elementary divisors, nonzero determinants and their valuations for all exponents. An independent integer resultant/binary gcd replay equated determinant valuation and binary nullity for both families at 1≤r≤6 (orders through 65). The replay is a check of small cases, not the all-exponent proof.
residual_risks: Only the prime two and the two stated odd-order families are classified; no full Smith form or other-prime claim is validated.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported contribution is the uniform exact two-primary lattice classification at both power-of-two-neighbor orders. The circulant, the determinant resultant, older parity/factorization relations, and finite determinant entries are not new. Since exact determinant valuations together with the easily recoverable mod-two nullity would imply the Smith factors, the comparison included scalar determinant literature rather than requiring prior work to use Smith terminology. No inspected source establishes the two-family formula or a theorem implying it; access to two relevant determinant papers limits historical priority claims.
residual_risks: Relevant full determinant/congruence results in the 1997 and 2005 papers were not available to this review. An earlier uniform valuation identity combined with binary nullity would be substantive prior coverage even if not labeled a Smith result.

value.rationale: The natural orders next to powers of two give exact lattice information for a classical determinant family. The classification tells not merely whether two divides, but exactly how many independent order-two cokernel summands occur and that no order-four or higher summands survive, uniformly in r and with the parity contrast between the families. The integral proof explains why binary root overlap never lifts to a higher valuation in these cases.
residual_risks: No claim to classify two-adic behavior at arbitrary odd orders or to refine the odd-primary factors.
